title: Preflight Ops Gate: Terraform + Live Validator for VPC Private Installs
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a dual-path preflight validation that combines Terraform/IaC assertions with a live validator CLI to catch customer-side failures before Private (VPC) installs.

Background: On recent Private installs we've seen recurring failures caused by insufficient cloud quotas (ENIs, GPUs, EIPs), mis-scoped IAM roles, missing DNS forwarding or private hosted zone configuration, and region-specific GPU capacity shortages. Existing terraform pre-checks are fragmented across customer guides and ad-hoc scripts. This ticket defines and implements an opinionated, repeatable preflight gate delivered as: (1) a Terraform module with plan-time assertions and reporting, and (2) a standalone 'redwood-preflight' binary that runs live API checks (quotas, IAM policy simulation, DNS resolution, GPU availability) and emits machine-readable results for automation and human guidance.

Scope:
- Terraform module (redwood/preflight) to be consumed in customer root module; validates provider versions, backend config, required variables, and performs plan-time data sources checks where possible (e.g., aws_servicequotas for static quota values).
- Live validator CLI (Go) that calls cloud provider APIs to verify dynamic/soft-state items that Terraform cannot reliably assert: current quota usage vs limits, available GPU instance capacity per AZ, IAM assume-role/test policies using policy simulator, and DNS reachability tests for private hosted zones / inbound endpoints.
- A standardized JSON output schema and exit codes to integrate with onboarding pipelines and the Console preinstall checklist.
- Runbooks and clear remediation messages for customers and SREs.

Constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Using only Terraform data sources avoids extra binaries but cannot detect transient capacity (e.g., no available p4 instances in a zone). Chosen hybrid approach: Terraform for static checks; CLI for dynamic checks.
- Provider coverage: MVP targets AWS and GCP. Azure planned as follow-up.
- Permission model: live validator requires read-only API permissions; IAM simulation requires permission to call the simulator APIs. Avoid requesting admin-level privileges in docs.

Deliverables:
- redwood/preflight Terraform module (registry-style) with examples for common topologies (single AZ, multi-AZ, private hosted zone).
- redwood-preflight CLI with subcommands: check-quotas, check-iam, check-dns, check-gpu, summary.
- JSON schema for results and Console integration RFC.
- Documentation (Quickstart + troubleshooting) and customer-facing remediation suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to internal registry and verified against three canonical test accounts (small, medium, enterprise).
redwood-preflight CLI can run against AWS and GCP and returns standard JSON output and exit codes documented in RFC.

Checks implemented: ENI/EIP/subnet quotas, service quotas (including GPU instance quota), IAM role/policy simulation, DNS private-hosted-zone resolution or inbound endpoint reachability, CIDR overlap detection.
Automated test harness that can run validator against mocked cloud APIs for CI with >90% coverage for edge cases.
Console preinstall UI can consume the JSON output and surface human-readable remediation steps for each failed check.
